daily.title: The Quiet Revolution of Urban Beekeeping
passage: A

Cities are sometimes imagined as places hostile to wildlife, yet a growing body of evidence suggests that some species do exceptionally well in urban environments. Among the most surprising of these urban adapters is the honeybee. Across Europe, North America and parts of Asia, beekeepers are placing hives on rooftops, in allotments, beside railway lines and inside community gardens, creating a movement that researchers have begun to describe as a quiet revolution in the way cities relate to nature.
B

The scale of the trend is hard to overstate. In London alone, the number of registered beekeepers has more than tripled over the last fifteen years, and similar growth has been reported in Paris, Berlin and New York. Industry estimates suggest that there are now well over fifty thousand managed urban hives across these four cities. Although exact figures vary because registration is voluntary, surveys of equipment suppliers consistently show a steady rise in sales of beginner kits, suggesting that the trend is not driven solely by established professionals.
C

Researchers have proposed several explanations for why bees thrive in towns. Urban areas offer an unusually long flowering season because parks, road verges and ornamental gardens contain plants selected to bloom at different times of the year. The heat trapped by buildings and pavements also raises overnight temperatures, allowing colonies to forage earlier in spring and later in autumn than they would in surrounding farmland. Crucially, urban environments tend to have a lower density of industrial farms, which means that the pesticide pressure experienced by foraging bees is often much reduced compared with the countryside.
D

The honey produced in cities has become a small but visible symbol of this movement. Urban honey frequently commands a premium price, partly because of its novelty and partly because some laboratory analyses have shown that it contains a wider range of pollen types than rural samples. Beekeepers describe their honey with vivid place names, often tied to a particular park, street or landmark, and consumers appear willing to pay several times the supermarket rate for jars that carry a recognisable local story. Small bakeries, restaurants and independent shops have been quick to incorporate urban honey into their products, reinforcing the sense that a city can produce something distinctive rather than simply consuming the output of distant rural areas.
E

The movement is not without concerns. Some entomologists caution that densely packed urban hives can compete with the wild solitary bees that already live in cities, potentially reducing the food available to those species. Others worry that beginners may abandon hives when colonies become aggressive or fail to survive the winter, leaving equipment to deteriorate in back gardens. Local authorities have responded with mixed strategies: some have issued formal guidelines on hive numbers per square kilometre, while others have left the question to neighbourhood associations. The regulatory landscape, in short, remains uneven.
F

Education has emerged as one of the most important responses to these challenges. Community workshops, run by experienced beekeepers in partnership with libraries and environmental groups, now teach newcomers how to inspect a colony, recognise common diseases and harvest honey without harming the bees. Several cities have also launched schemes that place hives in schools, where pupils monitor the insects as part of broader lessons on pollination, food systems and climate change. Early evaluations suggest that participants in these programmes retain a more accurate understanding of bee behaviour than people who learn only from online videos, although the long-term effects on actual beekeeping practice are still being studied.
G

For all the enthusiasm, the broader ecological significance of urban beekeeping remains a matter of debate. Honeybees are not native to many of the cities where they are now kept, and some ecologists argue that resources spent supporting managed colonies could be better directed at restoring wildflower habitat for native pollinators. Defenders counter that urban hives act as ambassadors, drawing public attention to the plight of pollinators in general, and that the honey produced provides a small economic incentive for city dwellers who might otherwise have little contact with agriculture. The two positions are not necessarily incompatible, but reconciling them will require careful monitoring of both managed and wild bee populations over the coming decade.
H

What is beyond doubt is that the appearance of hives on balconies and rooftops has changed the way many urban residents think about their environment. A beehive is a tangible, working reminder that food production does not end at the city boundary, and that even a small green space can host a complex web of relationships between insects, plants and people. Whether the trend expands, stabilises or fades, it has already left a clear mark on the cultural landscape of the modern city.

_oldDaily.title: The Rise of Urban Vertical Farming
passage: A

Vertical farming, the practice of growing crops in stacked layers inside controlled environments, has moved from science fiction to commercial reality in under two decades. Proponents argue that it answers three of agriculture's most pressing problems: land scarcity, water consumption and food miles.
B

Because crops are grown hydroponically — their roots bathed in nutrient-rich water rather than soil — vertical farms can use up to 95 per cent less water than conventional agriculture. Stacking growing trays also multiplies the productive area of a single urban plot many times over, and locating farms inside cities cuts the distance food travels to consumers dramatically.
C

Critics, however, point to the industry's Achilles' heel: energy. Replacing sunlight with LED lighting is expensive, and unless the electricity comes from renewable sources, the carbon footprint of a lettuce grown indoors can exceed that of one trucked in from a distant field. Several high-profile start-ups have collapsed after underestimating operating costs.
D

The sector's future most likely lies in a narrower niche than early evangelists imagined: high-value, fast-growing crops such as herbs and salad leaves, grown close to dense urban markets where freshness commands a premium.
E

label: Academic Task 1 - multi-country comparison across two time points

requirement: Select and report the main features, compare where relevant, write at least 150 words
选取并报告主要特征,在相关处进行比较,字数不少于 150 词
detail: You need an overview of the overall pattern, plus the most useful groupings. Norway and Australia rose moderately, South Korea rose sharply and overtook Norway, and Mexico stayed lowest while still growing. Pairing South Korea with Norway shows the leadership swap, while Australia and Mexico show a steady but smaller growth pattern.
你需要先给出整体趋势的概述,再按最有用的分组展开。挪威和澳大利亚涨幅较平缓,韩国涨幅最大并反超挪威,墨西哥起点最低但同样上升。把韩国与挪威配对可以突出排名变化,把澳大利亚与墨西哥配对可以呈现稳步上升的另一组。
pitfall: Do not list every figure separately or treat the task as four country stories. Do not invent causes, opinions, predictions or a conclusion that just repeats the overview.
不要逐国罗列所有数字,也不要把它写成四个国家的独立故事。不要编造原因、观点、预测,也不要写一段只重复概述的结尾。

label: Discussion essay with opinion
讨论类作文,需表明观点
requirement: Discuss both views and give your own opinion
讨论两种观点并给出你自己的看法
detail: The prompt asks you to present two contrasting positions on whether university students should study outside their main field. You must summarise both sides fairly, then state and justify your own view in the conclusion. A clear position is required, supported by reasons and examples drawn from real study or work contexts.
题目要求你呈现两种对比立场,关于大学生是否应学习主修以外的内容。你必须公平概括双方观点,然后在结尾表明并论证自己的看法。需要有明确立场,并用源自真实学习或工作情境的理由和例子支撑。
pitfall: Do not spend the whole essay on one view and ignore the other. Do not mention your opinion only in the introduction and leave it unsupported in a final paragraph.
不要整篇只写一种观点而忽略另一种。不要只在开头提及立场,却在结尾段不进行支撑论证。

text: Universities should require all students to take courses outside their main field, because broad learning produces more adaptable graduates.
大学应要求所有学生学习主修以外的课程,因为广博学习能培养更具适应力的毕业生。
note: This position lets you argue that interdisciplinary exposure builds critical thinking, supports innovation, and meets employer demand for flexible skills. It also gives you a clear structure. You can explain the broad-education view, acknowledge the specialisation case, then defend your own view with reasons and a short example.
这一立场让你论证跨学科接触能培养批判性思维,推动创新,契合雇主对灵活技能的需求。同时也能清晰安排结构,先解释广泛教育的观点,再承认专精的论点,最后用理由和简短例子捍卫自己的立场。

text: Students should be free to focus on their chosen specialisation, with optional access to other fields for those who want it.
学生应自由专注于所选专业,有需要者可以选修其他领域。
note: This route lets you defend depth over breadth while still appearing balanced. You acknowledge the value of other subjects, then explain why forced broad study is inefficient and why student choice preserves motivation. It suits prompts where you want a sharper, less common opinion that still respects the other side.
这条路线让你捍卫深度优于广度,同时仍显得平衡。你承认其他学科的价值,再解释为什么强制广泛学习效率不高,以及为什么学生自主选择能保护学习动力。它适合想要更鲜明且不常见立场,又仍尊重对方的题目。

text: Universities should blend both approaches by requiring a small core of outside subjects while keeping the main focus on specialisation.
大学应融合两种做法,要求少量主修以外的核心课,同时保留专业主修。
note: This balanced view is often the safest route for the Writing test because it lets you credit both sides and then explain a precise middle position. You can argue that a small, well-chosen outside core gives breadth without the costs of full broad study, and that free specialisation protects depth.
这种平衡观点在写作考试中常是最稳妥的路线,既肯定双方,又能阐明一个精确的中间立场。你可以论证少量精选的外围核心课带来广度,又避免完全广泛学习的代价,而自由的专业学习则保护了深度。

text: Overall, full-time higher education enrolment rose in all four countries between 2010 and 2020, with South Korea showing the steepest increase and overtaking Norway as the leader.
总体来看,2010 到 2020 年四国全日制高等教育入学率均有所上升,其中韩国增幅最大并反超挪威成为最高。
note: Framing the overview around the universal rise plus the South Korea-Norway leadership swap gives you one clear overall pattern. It then justifies a detail structure that contrasts the two leaders on one side and the two lower-ranked countries on the other.
把概述聚焦在四国共同上升以及韩国反超挪威这一整体走势,可以给出一个清晰的整体模式,也方便在细节段把两位领先国与两位较低国家分开对比。

text: Full-time higher education enrolment was higher in every country in 2020 than in 2010, with the largest jump in South Korea and the smallest in Mexico.
2020 年四国全日制高等教育入学率均高于 2010 年,韩国涨幅最大,墨西哥涨幅最小。
note: Leading with the universal increase highlights the most defensible overall pattern and lets the detail paragraphs rank the four growth rates. This structure keeps comparisons explicit and avoids four separate country stories.
先用四国共同上升作为整体模式,再在细节段按增幅大小排序比较,可以突出对比,也避免变成四个国家的独立叙述。

text: Between 2010 and 2020, every country saw a rise in full-time higher education enrolment, with South Korea overtaking Norway and Mexico staying the lowest throughout.
2010 至 2020 年,所有国家的全日制高等教育入学率均上升,韩国反超挪威,墨西哥始终最低。
note: Opening the overview with both the universal rise and the rank stability of Mexico gives two anchoring features. The detail paragraphs can then focus on the leadership change and on the consistent gap between the lower pair and the leaders.
概述同时点出共同上升和墨西哥始终最低这两个稳定特征,细节段就可以重点写排名变化,以及较低两国与领先国家之间持续存在的差距。

tag: Introduce the chart topic, time points and the four countries without giving all figures.
介绍图表主题、时间和四个国家,不给出全部数字。
text: The chart compares the share of 18- to 24-year-olds enrolled in full-time higher education in four countries in 2010 and 2020.
该图表比较了 2010 年和 2020 年四个国家 18 至 24 岁人群的全日制高等教育入学比例。
bullets: - State the four countries and the two reference years clearly.
example: Norway, South Korea, Australia and Mexico in 2010 and 2020.

tag: Give a source-grounded overview of the main pattern and ranking change.
给出基于数据的整体趋势概述和排名变化。
text: Enrolment rose in every country, and South Korea moved from third place to first.
四国入学率均上升,韩国从第三位升至第一位。
bullets: - All four countries recorded an increase between 2010 and 2020.
- South Korea overtook Norway to become the highest at 41% in 2020.
example: South Korea climbed from 28% to 41%, while Norway moved from 32% to 39%.

tag: Compare the two leading countries and their growth rates.
比较两个领先国家及其增长速度。
text: Norway and South Korea were the clear leaders, though South Korea grew much faster.
挪威和韩国明显领先,但韩国的增速远高于挪威。
bullets: - Norway rose by 7 percentage points from 32% to 39%.
- South Korea rose by 13 percentage points from 28% to 41%, the largest gain.
example: South Korea added roughly twice as many percentage points as Norway.

tag: Compare the two lower-ranked countries and their more modest growth.
比较排名较低的两国及其较平缓的增长。
text: Australia and Mexico also increased, but remained below the two leaders.
澳大利亚和墨西哥同样上升,但仍低于两位领先国家。
bullets: - Australia rose from 26% to 34%, gaining 8 percentage points.
- Mexico rose from 21% to 27%, staying the lowest throughout.
example: Mexico was about 12 percentage points below Norway in 2020.

tag: Paraphrase the task and identify the countries and years covered.
改写题目,点明所涉及的国家和年份。
text: The chart shows full-time higher education enrolment among 18- to 24-year-olds in four countries in 2010 and 2020.
该图表展示了 2010 年和 2020 年四个国家 18 至 24 岁人群的全日制高等教育入学率。
bullets: - Mention the four countries and the two years compared.

tag: Provide a source-grounded overview of the universal rise and the gap between countries.
给出基于数据的共同上升概述及国家间差距。
text: Enrolment was higher in 2020 than in 2010 in every country shown.
图中所有国家 2020 年的入学率均高于 2010 年。
bullets: - All four countries recorded an increase of at least 6 percentage points.
- The spread between the highest and lowest country widened only slightly.
example: The gap between leader and lowest country was 11 points in 2010 and 14 points in 2020.

tag: Compare the two countries with the largest increases.
比较增幅最大的两个国家。
text: South Korea and Australia recorded the strongest growth.
韩国和澳大利亚的增幅最为明显。
bullets: - South Korea rose 13 points from 28% to 41%, the largest gain.
- Australia rose 8 points from 26% to 34%, the second largest gain.
example: South Korea added about 5 percentage points more than Australia.

tag: Compare the two countries with the smallest increases and their stable ranking.
比较增幅最小的两个国家及其较稳定的排名。
text: Norway and Mexico showed more modest increases and kept their relative positions.
挪威和墨西哥增幅较平缓,相对位次基本未变。
bullets: - Norway rose 7 points from 32% to 39%, staying near the top.
- Mexico rose 6 points from 21% to 27%, staying at the bottom.
example: Mexico remained the lowest of the four in both years.

tag: Detail the leadership change between Norway and South Korea.
详细说明挪威和韩国之间的排名变化。
text: The most striking change was South Korea overtaking Norway to take the top position.
最显著的变化是韩国反超挪威升至首位。
bullets: - Norway led in 2010 at 32%, ahead of South Korea at 28%.
- South Korea led in 2020 at 41%, ahead of Norway at 39%.

tag: Compare the two lower-ranked countries with the leaders and note the persistent gap.
将排名较低的两国与领先国家比较,并指出持续存在的差距。
text: Australia and Mexico remained clearly below Norway and South Korea throughout the period.
澳大利亚和墨西哥在整个时期内仍明显低于挪威和韩国。

review.WF_T2_ESSAY: It is often debated whether secondary school students should take part-time jobs. While some believe such work is essential preparation for adult life, others argue that it distracts teenagers from their academic and extracurricular priorities. In my opinion, part-time employment can be valuable if carefully managed, but it should never take precedence over education. On the one hand, supporters of part-time work argue that it provides practical experience that schools cannot offer. Holding a job helps young people develop responsibility, time management, and communication skills. For example, working in a café or retail store teaches teenagers how to deal with customers, handle money, and work in a team. These experiences can boost confidence and make them more competitive in the future job market. Moreover, earning their own money encourages financial awareness and independence, which are crucial for adulthood1. On the other hand, opponents contend that studying and extracurricular activities should come first. Secondary school is a critical period for building academic foundations, and poor grades can limit future opportunities. A part-time job, especially one with long or late hours, can lead to fatigue, stress, and reduced concentration in class. Teenagers may also miss out on sports, clubs, or volunteering, which also foster valuable skills. In some cases, employers may exploit young workers with low pay and poor conditions. In my view, a balanced approach is best2. Part-time work should be optional and limited—perhaps a few hours on weekends or during holidays. It should complement, not compete with, schooling. Parents and schools can guide students toward jobs that align with their interests or career goals, and ensure that academic performance does not suffer. If a student is struggling at school, work should be postponed. In conclusion, while part-time jobs can help prepare teenagers for working life, they are not essential for everyone. The priority must remain education and healthy development. With sensible limits and proper support, part-time work can be a positive experience rather than a distraction3.

monarch.title: The Migration of Monarch Butterflies
passage: Every autumn, millions of monarch butterflies embark on one of the most remarkable journeys in the natural world. Leaving the cooling forests of southern Canada and the northern United States, they travel up to 4,000 kilometres to reach the warm mountain forests of central Mexico, where they spend the winter.

What makes the migration so extraordinary is that no single butterfly completes the round trip. The insects that fly south in the autumn are three or four generations removed from those that made the journey the previous year, yet they return to the very same groves of trees — sometimes even the same individual trees — that their ancestors used. How they achieve this has puzzled scientists for decades.

Research suggests that the butterflies rely on more than one method of navigation. They appear to use the position of the sun as a compass, correcting for the way it moves across the sky during the day with the help of an internal clock. In addition, experiments indicate that they can sense the Earth's magnetic field, which may guide them on cloudy days when the sun is hidden.

The Mexican overwintering sites themselves were unknown to scientists until relatively recently. Although local communities had long been aware of the butterflies, the location of the main colonies was only formally documented by researchers in 1975. Today these sites are protected, but the species still faces threats from habitat loss and a changing climate.

_oldDaily.title: The Development of Writing Systems
passage: A

The invention of writing is widely regarded as one of humanity's most transformative achievements. The earliest known writing systems emerged independently in at least three regions: Mesopotamia around 3200 BCE, Egypt shortly thereafter, and China by approximately 1200 BCE. Each system arose in response to specific administrative and social needs, though the paths they followed differed considerably.
B

In Mesopotamia, writing began as a system of accounting. Temple administrators needed to track goods — quantities of grain, numbers of livestock, and volumes of trade. The earliest tablets from Uruk contain nothing resembling literature or history; they are inventories and receipts. Over several centuries, these pictographic symbols became increasingly abstract, evolving into the wedge-shaped marks we call cuneiform. Only after the system had been in use for administrative purposes for roughly 500 years did scribes begin recording myths, laws, and diplomatic correspondence.
C

Egyptian hieroglyphs present a different developmental pattern. From their earliest appearance, hieroglyphs served both practical and ceremonial functions. Royal monuments bore inscriptions that combined record-keeping with religious and political propaganda. The Egyptians also developed cursive scripts — hieratic and later demotic — for everyday administrative use, while reserving the elaborate hieroglyphic forms for formal contexts.
D

Chinese writing followed yet another trajectory. The earliest confirmed Chinese characters appear on oracle bones used for divination during the Shang dynasty. These inscriptions record questions posed to ancestors and deities about warfare, harvests, and royal health. The system was already quite sophisticated by the time of these earliest surviving examples, suggesting an earlier developmental phase that has not been preserved.
E

What these three traditions share is a common pattern: writing systems tend to begin with narrow, specialized uses before expanding to serve broader communicative purposes. The technology of writing, once invented, proved remarkably adaptable, eventually transforming not just administration but human thought itself.
